secondary_factors: General equity volatility and recession fears. OPEC considering additional 1.5M bpd cut and market unsure Russia would cooperate
store_description: No distinct ConocoPhillips headline in the 3-day window. The best explanation is oil-market stress with Wood Mackenzie estimating global oil demand in the quarter could fall by about 2.7M bpd YoY while OPEC was considering deeper cuts and Russia cooperation was uncertain.

primary_cause: COVID-driven fear of hit to Disney parks cruises theatrical releases and ESPN-related ad demand
secondary_factors: Broad market drop and travel-related selling. Flybe collapsed Mar 5 adding to travel sector fear
store_description: This looks more like an exposure trade than a Disney-specific event. By March 5 investors could see that businesses tied to travel and gatherings were breaking down and Disney had unusually high sensitivity through parks resorts cruises film distribution and live sports.

primary_cause: COVID-related global auto demand and supply-chain fears. China passenger-car sales had plunged about 92% in early February
secondary_factors: Cyclical-stock selloff and recession concerns. Highly cyclical manufacturer with big fixed costs and international exposure
store_description: The strongest explanation is macro but sector-specific. China passenger-car sales had plunged about 92% in early February showing what a virus shock could do to auto demand and investors were extrapolating that risk globally. GM was repriced lower as those fears intensified.

secondary_factors: Credit-quality fears tied to possible recession and virus shock. Reuters: S&P banks index down 4.7% on Mar 6
store_description: No Wells Fargo-only negative headline. The more convincing driver is the rate shock with the 10-year Treasury yield falling below 1% for the first time after the Fed emergency cut. Bank shares were hit as investors priced weaker lending spreads and higher economic risk.

primary_cause: Lower-rate and flatter-curve pressure on bank earnings after Fed emergency 50bp cut and historic Treasury rally
secondary_factors: Broader recession fears and sector-wide bank selling
store_description: No meaningful US Bancorp-specific catalyst in the 3-day window. Classic regional-bank NIM move as yields collapsed and the market priced more easing. Investors marked down earnings power for spread lenders such as USB.

secondary_factors: No clear company-specific negative catalyst found. Escalating COVID uncertainty after post-Fed-cut selloff resumed

secondary_factors: Broad Nasdaq and risk-off pressure
store_description: No Micron-only news item that explains the drop better than sector pressure. Given Micron's sensitivity to memory pricing electronics demand and global supply chains the most likely driver was intensifying concern that coronavirus would hit both production and end markets.

primary_cause: Macro industrial slowdown fears from COVID. Tied to industrial production manufacturing energy and healthcare demand
secondary_factors: Broad market selloff. Had been hitting record highs in mid-Feb on upbeat growth commentary making reversal sharper
store_description: Linde sold off as the market began pricing a global activity freeze. No company-specific negative update in the 3-day window making a macro and industrial explanation the best-supported one. The stock had been at record highs in mid-February which made the reversal more pronounced.

secondary_factors: Recession and credit-loss fears
store_description: No JPM-specific bombshell in the prior 3 days. The market was rapidly repricing large banks for lower net interest income and higher credit stress as Treasury yields cratered and investors interpreted the Fed emergency cut as confirmation that the virus shock could be severe.

primary_cause: No meaningful Intuit-specific headline. Broad software and growth multiple compression in risk-off trading
secondary_factors: Indiscriminate cutting of premium-multiple tech and software names amid escalating coronavirus uncertainty
store_description: No evidence of a fresh Intuit-specific negative development immediately before the drop. Investors were indiscriminately cutting exposure to premium-multiple tech and software names amid escalating coronavirus uncertainty and a renewed market slide.

primary_cause: Aviation and travel collapse fears hitting GE's most important profit engine. Global air travel demand collapsing
secondary_factors: Industrial recession concerns and general market selloff. Drop larger than many industrial peers due to aviation dependence
store_description: GE's drop was larger than many industrial peers because its earnings quality depended heavily on aviation a business suddenly facing a severe traffic and aftermarket shock. The market had enough information by March 6 to start repricing GE for a major hit to engine deliveries services and airline customer health.

primary_cause: Oil-price weakness from COVID demand destruction and OPEC+ uncertainty. OPEC+ debating additional 1.5M bpd cut while demand estimates collapsing
secondary_factors: Broad equity selloff. Before full Saudi-Russia price war erupted after close on Mar 6
store_description: No fresh Exxon-specific catalyst. The evidence points to crude-price pressure with OPEC+ debating deeper cuts while demand estimates were collapsing. This directly hurt integrated oils like Exxon even before the full Saudi-Russia price war erupted after the close on March 6.

primary_cause: No new Salesforce-specific development. Broad software multiple compression and macro uncertainty
secondary_factors: Risk-off selling in software and growth equities amid mounting concern over enterprise spending
store_description: This looks like a macro and valuation decline rather than a CRM-specific reaction. As investors questioned how COVID might affect corporate budgets and near-term growth assumptions richly valued enterprise-software names sold off with the wider tech complex.

primary_cause: Breakdown of OPEC+ Russia talks on March 6. Russia refused to back deeper cuts. With demand already weakening sharply collapse of cooperation made crude outlook materially worse
secondary_factors: COVID demand destruction and broader market selloff
store_description: This is stronger than the March 5 COP explanation because there was a major sector catalyst on the day. Russia declined to go along with the deeper cuts OPEC wanted. With demand already weakening sharply the collapse of OPEC+ cooperation made the outlook for crude materially worse.

primary_cause: Consumer-credit and recession fears plus lower-rate pressure after Fed emergency cut
secondary_factors: Broad bank and financial selloff. Travel and spending slowdown for card portfolios
store_description: No Capital One-specific headline in the 3-day window. Investors were simultaneously pricing lower funding spreads and a possible deterioration in card and consumer loan credit which made lenders like COF especially sensitive to a fast-moving virus scare.

primary_cause: Rate and yield collapse hurting bank earnings outlook. Emergency Fed cut sub-1% 10-year bank-index weakness on Mar 6
secondary_factors: Recession and credit-loss fears. Citi global card and corporate exposure added cross-border slowdown sensitivity
store_description: No new Citi-only event. The market was rapidly marking down large banks as falling yields threatened net interest revenue while coronavirus raised the probability of weaker loan demand and higher credit costs.

secondary_factors: Broader financial-sector weakness
store_description: BlackRock's decline is best explained by its exposure to market levels and investor sentiment rather than a company event. As equities fell and volatility surged the market discounted lower asset-based fees and tougher near-term flows for managers like BLK.

secondary_factors: Lower market levels potentially pressuring fee-linked businesses
store_description: No BNY Mellon-specific catalyst. BK is less pure-credit-sensitive than some banks but still exposed to lower rates and weaker market activity. With Treasury yields at record lows and financials broadly under pressure BK sold off alongside the rest of the sector.

secondary_factors: Recession and credit fears and sector-wide selling. Reuters: long-dated yield declines hammering financials
store_description: No Bank of America-specific negative headline in the prior 3 days. The strongest explanation is the same one hitting all money-center banks: a sharp reset lower in rate expectations and a flight to Treasuries that pushed the 10-year yield below 1% threatening earnings power.

secondary_factors: Classic early-COVID de-rating of premium software. Investors repricing growth assumptions and less willing to pay high multiples
